# ULong 〔BlitzLLVM〕

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [BlitzBasic](BlitzBasic) · [Math](BlitzBasic-Math)

</div>


## Command Syntax

```blitzbasic
ULong:Int32 value:Float32
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | Float32 | required | A number or a text with a number in it. |

**Returns:** The ULong.

## Description

**〔BlitzLLVM〕** This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

<!-- AUTOGENERATED COPYRIGHT HEADER START -->
Converts a number or a text to a ULong, a 64-bit integer from 0 to 18446744073709551615. This is a BlitzLLVM extension: the originals only know `Int` and `Float`. A whole number below 0 keeps its lowest 64 bits (`ULong(-1)` is 18446744073709551615), a real is rounded to the nearest whole number (halves go to the even one) and stops at 0 or the largest number if it is outside. Use [SatULong](SatULong) to stop whole numbers below 0 at 0 as well. A ULong is compared, divided and shifted right without a sign, and `Abs` and `Sgn` see it as never negative.

## Differences

* Not in the originals, which have no integers of other sizes.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Print ULong(-1)
Print ULong(3000000000.0)
Print ULong(-1) Shr 60
Print Min(ULong(-1), ULong(5))
```

```text
18446744073709551615
3000000000
15
5
```
